questions.text: Choose the option that best replaces the underlined segment to make the sentence grammatically correct. If the sentence is correct, select 'No improvement'. Most employees **would rather to work** from home than commute daily.
questions.solution: Shortcut: 'Would rather' is a 'bare infinitive' trigger. It is *always* followed by V1 (base form) without 'to'. Eliminate Option B (gerund) and the original sentence (to + V1). Option C changes the structure to 'would prefer to' which is grammatically correct but Option A is the direct correction of the specific modal structure used. Full Solution: The modal phrase 'would rather' (or 'had rather') must be followed by the bare infinitive (V1). The use of 'to' after 'rather' is a classic error. Correct form: 'would rather work'. Option A provides this exact correction. Option C ('would prefer to work') is grammatically valid but alters the phrasing unnecessarily; the most appropriate improvement retaining the original modal is Option A.

questions.text: Statements: Some Pens are Pencils. All Pencils are Erasers. No Eraser is a Sharpener. Conclusions: I. Some Pens are not Sharpeners. II. All Pencils can never be Sharpeners.

options.label: B
options.text: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

options.label: D
options.text: Both Conclusions I and II follow

questions.solution: Shortcut: Apply chain rules: Some + All = Some; Some + No = Some Not; All + No = No. Full: Some Pens are Pencils + All Pencils are Erasers ⇒ Some Pens are Erasers. This + No Eraser is Sharpener ⇒ Some Pens are not Sharpeners (I follows). All Pencils are Erasers + No Eraser is Sharpener ⇒ No Pencil is Sharpener ⇒ All Pencils can never be Sharpeners (II follows).

questions.text: Ravi starts from point A and walks 10 km north. He then turns right and walks 5 km. Next, he turns left and walks 8 km. Finally, he turns right and walks 6 km. In which direction is his final position with respect to the starting point A?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Track net horizontal (east-west) and vertical (north-south) displacements. North 10 → +10 N. Right (east) 5 → +5 E. Left (north) 8 → +8 N. Right (east) 6 → +6 E. Net: 11 km East, 18 km North → North-East. Full steps: Represent each move as a vector, sum the components, and determine the quadrant of the resultant vector.

questions.text: Direction: In the following sentence, a segment is underlined. Choose the option that best replaces the underlined segment to make the sentence grammatically correct. If the sentence is correct, select 'No improvement'. Scarcely had the announcement **been made than** the crowd dispersed in an orderly manner.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Spot the negative adverbial 'Scarcely' at the start. Rule 1: It triggers inversion (Had the announcement). Rule 2: It pairs ONLY with 'when' (never 'than'). Eliminate Option B (uses 'than'). Rule 3: 'Announcement' receives the action → Passive voice needed ('been made'). Eliminate Option C (active 'made'). Option A satisfies both inversion structure and correct conjunction. Full Solution: The sentence uses the 'Scarcely... when' correlative structure requiring subject-auxiliary inversion ('had the announcement'). Since the announcement is made by someone, passive voice ('been made') is mandatory. 'Than' is used only with 'No sooner'. Thus, 'been made when' is the grammatically correct replacement.

questions.text: Statements: Some Pens are Pencils. All Pencils are Erasers. No Eraser is a Sharpener. Conclusions: I. Some Pens are not Sharpeners. II. All Pencils being Sharpeners is a possibility.

options.label: C
options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow

options.label: D
options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows

questions.solution: Shortcut: Use the 'Some + All = Some' and 'Some + No = Some Not' rules. For Possibility, check if the conclusion contradicts a definite 'No' statement. If 'No A is B', then 'All A being B' is impossible. Full Solution: From 'Some Pens are Pencils' and 'All Pencils are Erasers', we get 'Some Pens are Erasers'. Combining 'Some Pens are Erasers' with 'No Eraser is a Sharpener' gives 'Some Pens are not Sharpeners' (Conclusion I follows). For Conclusion II: 'All Pencils are Erasers' + 'No Eraser is Sharpener' ⇒ 'No Pencil is Sharpener'. Since 'No Pencil is Sharpener' is definite, the possibility 'All Pencils being Sharpeners' cannot exist. Thus, only Conclusion I follows.

questions.text: A sum of money becomes 1.44 times of itself in 2 years at compound interest compounded annually. What is the annual rate of interest?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Since the amount is 1.44 times the principal after 2 years, (1 + R/100)^2 = 1.44. Taking square root gives 1 + R/100 = 1.2, so R = 20%. Full solution: Let principal be P. Amount after 2 years = P(1 + R/100)^2 = 1.44P. Hence (1 + R/100)^2 = 1.44. Taking square root, 1 + R/100 = 1.2 => R/100 = 0.2 => R = 20%.

questions.text: A shopkeeper marks an article 40% above its cost price. He allows a discount of 15% on the marked price and then offers an additional 5% discount on the reduced price for cash payment. What is his overall profit percentage?

Given below are two statements. Choose the starter(s) that can combine them into a single sentence without changing the meaning. 1. The interest rates have been hiked by the central bank for the third time this year. 2. The real estate sector is witnessing a slowdown in demand for housing loans. Starters: (i) Since the interest rates have been hiked... (ii) Although the interest rates have been hiked... (iii) With the interest rates having been hiked...
questions.solution: Shortcut: Check logical relationship. Statement 1 (Rate Hike) is the CAUSE; Statement 2 (Slowdown) is the EFFECT. Starters showing Cause/Effect or Concession work. (i) 'Since' = Cause (Works). (ii) 'Although' = Contrast (Fails: Hike causes slowdown, they don't contrast). (iii) 'With... hiked' = Participle phrase showing reason/circumstance (Works). Full Solution: The relationship is Cause (Rate Hike) -> Effect (Slowdown). Starter (i) 'Since' correctly establishes causality. Starter (ii) 'Although' implies an unexpected contrast (e.g., 'Although rates hiked, demand rose'), which contradicts the economic logic here. Starter (iii) 'With the interest rates having been hiked' functions as an absolute phrase denoting the prevailing circumstance/reason, effectively combining the sentences. Thus, only (i) and (iii) are valid.

questions.text: A and B start a business. A invests Rs. 30,000 for the whole year. B invests Rs. 45,000 for the first 8 months and then withdraws Rs. 15,000 for the remaining 4 months. If the total profit at the end of the year is Rs. 84,000, what is B's share?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Compute capital‑months: A = 30,000 × 12 = 3,60,000; B = 45,000 × 8 + 30,000 × 4 = 3,60,000 + 1,20,000 = 4,80,000. Ratio A:B = 3:4. B's share = 4/7 × 84,000 = 48,000. Full method: Profit is divided in proportion to the product of capital and time. Calculate each partner's capital‑time, form the ratio, then allocate the total profit accordingly.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following alphanumeric series? A2, C4, E8, G16, ?
questions.solution: The letters follow alternate alphabetical order: A, C, E, G, so the next letter is I (skipping one each time). The numbers double each step: 2, 4, 8, 16, so the next number is 32. Combining these gives I32 as the missing term.

questions.text: In the following question, the symbols @, #, $, %, and & are used with the following meanings: 'P @ Q' means 'P is not smaller than Q' (P ≥ Q) 'P # Q' means 'P is neither greater than nor equal to Q' (P < Q) 'P $ Q' means 'P is neither smaller than nor equal to Q' (P > Q) 'P % Q' means 'P is not greater than Q' (P ≤ Q) 'P & Q' means 'P is neither greater than nor smaller than Q' (P = Q) Statement: A @ B, B # C, C $ D, D % E Conclusions: I. A $ D (A > D) II. C $ E (C > E)

options.label: C
options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow

options.label: D
options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows

questions.solution: Shortcut: Decode symbols to standard signs (≥, <, >, ≤, =). Form a chain: A ≥ B < C > D ≤ E. Check conclusions by tracing the chain. If the direction of signs reverses (e.g., ≥ then <, or > then ≤), no definite relation exists between those endpoints. Full Solution: Decoding gives A ≥ B, B < C, C > D, D ≤ E. Combining: A ≥ B < C > D ≤ E. For Conclusion I (A > D): Path is A ≥ B < C > D. Signs change from ≥ to < to >, so relation between A and D cannot be established. For Conclusion II (C > E): Path is C > D ≤ E. Signs change from > to ≤, so relation between C and E cannot be established. Hence, neither conclusion follows.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. The manager asked the HR department to ______ the employees **of** the new appraisal guidelines before the quarterly review.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use the 'Praise/Price' mnemonic. **Appraise** (contains 'praise') = to evaluate value/performance. **Apprise** (sounds like 'a-prize' -> info) = to inform/notify. The context 'guidelines' and the preposition 'of' after the blank ('apprise someone *of* something') confirms 'inform'. Full Solution: 'Appraise' means to assess the value or quality of something (e.g., appraise property). 'Apprise' means to inform or tell someone (e.g., apprise him of the facts). The sentence structure 'apprise the employees *of* the guidelines' requires the verb 'apprise'. Option A is the common confusion pair. Option C is a non-standard spelling. Option D uses the wrong verb with the preposition 'of'.

questions.text: Two trains of lengths 140 m and 210 m are running on parallel tracks in opposite directions. The speed of the shorter train is 54 km/h. If they cross each other completely in 10 seconds, what is the speed of the longer train?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Relative Speed (km/h) = (Sum of lengths in metres × 18) / (Time in seconds × 5). Here, Relative Speed = (350 × 18) / (10 × 5) = 126 km/h. Speed of longer train = 126 − 54 = 72 km/h. Step-by-step: Total distance = 140 + 210 = 350 m. Time = 10 s. Relative speed = 350/10 = 35 m/s. Convert to km/h: 35 × 18/5 = 126 km/h. Since directions are opposite, relative speed = Sum of speeds. Speed of longer train = 126 − 54 = 72 km/h.

questions.text: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'. Neither the Finance Minister nor the senior bureaucrats **was** available for comment on the new policy directive.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Spot the correlative conjunction 'Neither... nor'. Apply the Proximity Rule: the verb must agree with the subject nearest to it ('senior bureaucrats' – Plural). The singular verb 'was' is incorrect; it should be 'were'. Full Solution: In constructions with 'Neither... nor' or 'Either... or', the verb agrees with the noun/pronoun closest to it (Proximity Rule). Here, the nearest subject is 'senior bureaucrats' (Plural). Therefore, the plural verb 'were' is required. Segment C ('was available for comment') contains the Subject-Verb Agreement error.
questions.topic: Error Spotting - Subject Verb Agreement (Proximity Rule)

questions.text: A contractor employs 12 men and 18 women to complete a work in 20 days. The efficiency of a man is 1.5 times that of a woman. After 8 days, 4 men leave and 6 women join. In how many more days will the remaining work be finished?
questions.solution: Shortcut: The total efficiency before and after the change remains 36 units/day, so remaining days = total days – days elapsed = 20 – 8 = 12 days. Full: Let woman’s efficiency = 1 unit/day, man’s = 1.5 units/day. Initial daily work = 12×1.5 + 18×1 = 36 units. Total work = 36×20 = 720 units. Work done in 8 days = 36×8 = 288 units. Remaining = 432 units. New daily work = 8×1.5 + 24×1 = 36 units. Days needed = 432/36 = 12 days.
